frozenCriterion.statement: recommend only if the top-ranked action's risk upper bound is at most tau; unchanged by this analysis

counts.note: A forced choice with no observed introduction is NOT thereby safe: the observation covers the sampled member worlds of one class under one evaluator.

distributions.modelEstimatedQuantities: estimate, spread, upperBound and expectedRegret are MODEL OUTPUTS for the top-ranked action; they are not observed outcomes

discrimination.target: forced-choice class introduces against S0 or Nexus (observed outcome)

riskCoverage.label: POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC
riskCoverage.ordering: classes ordered by the frozen risk upper bound of the frozen top-ranked action; no threshold other than the frozen tau=0.2 was ever applied by the policy
riskCoverage.warning: Descriptive curve on a spent population. No point on it is a proposed operating point. The class-level bounds treat classes as independent; classes cluster by origin family, so they are optimistic.

breakdowns.horizonEffect: NOT_ESTIMABLE: every class has the same horizon band

riskEstimate.target: action is catastrophic in at least one member world of the class
riskEstimate.scope: This calibrates the per-action CATASTROPHE estimate. It is not a calibration of the probability that a recommendation INTRODUCES a catastrophe against a comparator, which the model does not estimate.

bagSpreadUncertainty.reason: No source-defined calibration metric exists for the bag-spread bound (mean + 1 sd across 10 family-bootstrap bags). It is a heuristic margin, not a calibrated interval, and is not assumed calibrated.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_boundVersusObservedR.note: Descriptive only: how often actions in each bound bin were catastrophic in some member. It does not verify the bound as a confidence statement.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_selectedActions.note: Model-estimated sums against observed counts for the top-ranked action of each class. Selection of the minimum-risk action could bias estimates downward (optimism); this checks the direction.

introductionVersusCatastrophe.note: The estimator targets catastrophe; the qualification gate counts introductions. A catastrophic choice is not an introduction when the comparator set is also catastrophic in that member world.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_withinMenuDiscrimina.note: Does the estimate order the actions of ONE menu correctly? Calibration across menus does not imply this.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_sharpness.note: How low does the estimate go for actions that were never catastrophic in any sampled member, and how often would the frozen criterion admit each kind of action?

matchedCohorts.note: Same classes for every policy. SK1 chose which classes to accept; the comparators did not. The ACCEPTED cohort therefore shows whether the kernel's gain there is more than a selection of classes that are easy for everyone.

assuranceArithmetic.note: Decided-class counts needed for a one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound, assuming independent decisions. Clustered data need more; the design effect must be estimated prospectively.

exposureAdjusted.note: Denominators restricted to accepted decisions whose set differs from the comparator set.

POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_designEffect.indicator: forced-choice class introduces against S0 or Nexus (all 600 classes, 39 events)
POST_HOC_DIAGNOSTIC_designEffect.note: Estimated on a spent population with few events; use only to size a future campaign, and re-estimate on fresh EXPLORATION data before any freeze.
